name: make
notes: AOSP does not carry make under platform/external; it carries GNU make source under toolchain/make and prebuilts under platform/prebuilts/build-tools.
The Gitiles +archive gzip hash is not stable across downloads, so the recipe pins the exact commit in the URL instead of using an archive checksum.
This recipe follows Android.bp's cc_binary_host source list so make can bootstrap without requiring an existing make executable.
Windows intentionally uses the POSIX-like musl config path rather than the upstream Win32 make path so failures expose CRT/PAL gaps.

make is not Windows-specific: tools/crt-port-build.py's build_port() unconditionally builds and installs this port before any 'configure'-system recipe on every host (not gated on target_os), and make_env() prefers the freshly-built PORT_PREFIX/bin/make over host make via $MAKE on all three OSes. So this project's own make has already driven every real ./configure && make && make install run for zlib/libpng/libffi on both Linux and macOS, all confirmed passing by the user on real hardware -- see those recipes' own status. Kept at manual-pass (matching Windows) rather than a higher tier since no standalone make --version/$(wildcard ...)-style direct check has been separately recorded for Linux/macOS, only its indirect, repeated use as the build driver for other ports.

windows target_overrides.env.LDFLAGS=-Wl,--stack,16777216 added 2026-08-24, found porting freetype: this project's own make.exe, linked with ld.lld's plain PE default stack reserve (1 MiB, the same default a real link.exe would also give an unadorned executable), segfaults completely silently (exit 139, zero stdout/stderr, deterministic and reproducible) partway through reading freetype's own unusually large, deeply cross-including hand-rolled Makefile tree (dozens of src/*/module.mk + rules.mk files, each contributing to a large combined variable/rule graph) -- every other Windows configure-based recipe this project has ported so far (curl/mbedTLS/libpng/pcre2/xz/zlib/libffi/expat/wayland) uses a far flatter, smaller Automake-style Makefile and never came close to exhausting a 1 MiB stack during GNU Make's own recursive rule/variable evaluation. Root-caused by relinking a copy of the already-built make.exe objects with a deliberately oversized 16 MiB stack reserve (`-Wl,--stack,16777216`, ld.lld/GNU-ld syntax) and confirming that copy parses and dry-runs (`make -n`) the exact same freetype Makefile tree cleanly -- a real stack-overflow, not a logic bug, and the fix (relink make itself with more stack headroom) is general: it costs nothing for every simpler recipe already verified working, and unblocks any future recipe with an equally large native Makefile graph.

windows target_overrides.cflags=-DHAVE_DOS_PATHS=1 added 2026-09-01, found porting ffmpeg: this project's own Windows make.exe, built without any Windows/DOS-path awareness at all (deliberate, per the 'POSIX-like musl config path ... so failures expose CRT/PAL gaps' note above -- soong/linux_musl/config.h leaves HAVE_DOS_PATHS undefined), has a real, general bug in its own path-absoluteness check: GNU Make re-execs itself (execve on its own argv[0]-derived path) whenever one of the Makefiles it read gets remade as a side effect of a rule during the same run -- ordinary, correct GNU Make behavior, not exotic -- and without HAVE_DOS_PATHS its absoluteness check only recognizes a leading '/' (src/makeint.h's own PATH_SEPARATOR_CHAR block, src/main.c ~line 1196/1589/1805), so a real, valid drive-letter path like 'C:/Users/.../make.exe' is treated as *relative* and silently corrupted by prepending make's own current directory ('make.exe: <cwd>/C:/Users/.../make.exe: No such file or directory'). No Windows recipe ported here before ffmpeg (curl/freetype/mbedtls/expat/xz/zlib/libffi, all flatter/non-restarting Makefile trees) ever exercised this self-restart code path, so the bug went undiscovered until FFmpeg's real, larger build graph (which regenerates *.version files that trigger exactly one restart) hit it directly. Fixed with a single, narrow -DHAVE_DOS_PATHS=1 cflag -- NOT by switching to the toolchain/make source tree's own soong/windows/config.h profile (which already exists, already defines HAVE_DOS_PATHS, but also switches the *source list* to native-Win32-specific files like w32/subproc/sub_proc.c instead of src/posixos.c -- a far larger, riskier change that would silently route around real CRT/PAL syscall paths this project's own musl-style profile exists specifically to keep exercised). HAVE_DOS_PATHS's own only other real effect on this exact source configuration is PATH_SEPARATOR_CHAR: ':' -> ';' (src/makeint.h) for parsing colon/semicolon-separated path lists (VPATH, $(wildcard) with -I-style lists, etc.) -- arguably a second real fix rather than a new risk, since a colon-separated convention was already ambiguous with every Windows drive-letter path this project's own env already threads through make (e.g. MAKE=C:/Users/...); PATH_SEPARATOR_CHAR itself was never independently overridden elsewhere in this recipe's own config layers. Re-verified for real (2026-09-01) by rebuilding and re-running each other Windows 'shared-pass' recipe's own real test with the new HAVE_DOS_PATHS make.exe: zlib/expat/xz/libffi/freetype all rebuild and re-test clean, no regression. mbedtls (and curl, which depends on it) initially failed to *link* on Windows ('duplicate symbol: __crt_wait32_shared' between libc.a and libmbedcrypto.dll.a when linking libmbedx509.dll) -- confirmed via a real A/B test (swapping a freshly-rebuilt pre-HAVE_DOS_PATHS make.exe binary back in place and re-running the exact same mbedtls rebuild) that this failure was pre-existing and NOT caused by this change: it reproduced byte-for-byte identically with the old make.exe. Root-caused and fixed separately the same day: porting/recipes/mbedtls-windows-exclude-symbols.rsp (this recipe's own known maintenance-debt hand-generated snapshot, see mbedtls.json's own notes) had simply drifted stale again -- regenerated (947 -> 1077 entries, confirmed strict superset via a real llvm-nm dump of libc.a), which included the newly-missing __crt_wait32_shared/__crt_wait32_timed_shared/cnd_wait/cnd_timedwait entries and fixed both mbedtls's own crypto-static/crypto-shared tests and curl's own link. curl's own separate, real 'Out of memory' runtime test failure (http-roundtrip-static, unrelated to mbedtls or HAVE_DOS_PATHS -- confirmed via the same A/B discipline plus a fully fresh zlib/curl rebuild) is tracked separately and does not block this change; see curl.json's own status/notes.
